Bug_Details:
Comparing protobuf fields of type String using reference equality Comparing strings with == is almost always an error, but it is an error 100% of
the time when one of the strings is a protobuf field. Additionally, protobuf
fields cannot be null, so Object.equals(Object) is always more correct.
Bug_Explanation: This bug is demonstrated by comparing the names of two Person objects. The bug occurs because the 'getName' method returns a String, which is a mutable object, and reference equality is used to compare the names. The expected behavior is that if two Person objects have the same name, then they should be considered equal. However, this bug is caused by the fact that reference equality is used, which compares the references (memory addresses) of the strings, not the actual content of the strings. To fix this bug, it is necessary to use the equals method to compare the strings, which compares the actual content of the strings.

This is a bug because it is almost always an error to compare strings using == in Java. The == operator checks if the two operands refer to the same object, not if they have the same value. Therefore, the method isNameEqual() will always return false, even when the names of the two persons are the same.
